ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m1.title: Divisibility by 5, 9 and 11
ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m1.body:
$495=5\cdot9\cdot11$ with $5,9,11$ pairwise coprime, so a number is divisible by $495$ iff it is divisible by $5$, $9$ and $11$.

Every term ends in $5$, so is divisible by $5$. A term with $2k$ digits is $55\cdot(1+100+\cdots+100^{k-1})$, a multiple of $55$ and so of $11$. A term with $2k+1$ digits equals $10\times(\text{previous term})+5$, so it leaves remainder $5$ on division by $11$. So we need an even number $2k$ of digits.

A term with $2k$ digits has digit sum $10k$, divisible by $9$ iff $9\mid k$. The smallest is $k=9$: the $18$-digit number made of eighteen $5$s.

**Answer: Yes, $555\,555\,555\,555\,555\,555$ (eighteen 5s)**

ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m2.title: Complete a square
ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m2.body:
$x^2+y^2+3xy=2015$ gives $3xy=2015-x^2-y^2$. Adding $2xy$:
$$5xy=2015-(x-y)^2\le2015,$$
with equality iff $x=y$. So $xy\le403$, and $x=y=\sqrt{403}$ satisfies the equation ($403+403+3\cdot403=2015$).

**Answer: 403**

ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m3.title: Pigeonhole and case analysis
ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m3.body:
(a) Split $90,\dots,99$ into the five pairs $(90,91),(92,93),(94,95),(96,97),(98,99)$. Six chosen numbers means some pair has both numbers chosen. Consecutive integers have highest common factor $1$, so these two are relatively prime.

(b) Yes. If at least two of the chosen numbers are even, they share the factor $2$. If at most one is even, then at least five are odd, and there are only five odd numbers $91,93,95,97,99$, so all five are chosen, including $93$ and $99$, which have common factor $3$.

**Answer: (a) proved; (b) yes.**

ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m4.title: Centre distance twice
ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m4.body:
Let the circles have centres $C$ (radius $a$) and $D$ (radius $b$).

For the tangent $AB$ ($A$ on the circle centre $C$, $B$ on the circle centre $D$): $CA\perp AB$, $DB\perp AB$. Let $F$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $CA$. Then $AFDB$ is a rectangle with $AF=b$, $FD=AB=16$, so $CF=a-b$ and
$$CD^2=16^2+(a-b)^2.$$
For the tangent $PQ$ (the internal tangent): $CP\perp PQ$, $DQ\perp PQ$. Let $G$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ onto the line $CP$ extended; the corresponding figure gives $PG=b$, $GD=PQ=14$, $CG=a+b$ and
$$CD^2=14^2+(a+b)^2.$$
Equating: $14^2+(a+b)^2=16^2+(a-b)^2$, so $(a+b)^2-(a-b)^2=256-196$, i.e. $4ab=60$ and $ab=15$. (The result is symmetric in $a,b$, so it does not matter which circle is which.) ∎

ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m5.title: Factorise
ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m5.body:
$a,b,c\in\{2,3,5,7\}$. If the equation has an integer root, the quadratic factorises over the integers as $(\text{lin})(\text{lin})$. As $c$ and $a$ are prime, the factorisation is either $(ax+c)(x+1)$ with $b=a+c$, or $(ax+1)(x+c)$ with $b=ac+1$ (all coefficients are positive, so the roots are negative integers).

- $b=a+c$ prime: one of $a,c$ must be $2$ (else $b$ is even and $>2$). Triples $(a,b,c)$: $(2,5,3),(2,7,5),(3,5,2),(5,7,2)$.
- $b=ac+1$ prime: $ac$ even, so one of $a,c$ is $2$. Triples: $(2,5,2),(2,7,3),(3,7,2)$.

No triple is in both lists, so there are $7$ equations.

**Answer: 7**

ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m6.title: Angle sum in a quadrilateral
ukmt-maclaurin-2015-m6.body:
Let $\alpha=\frac{360^\circ}{n}$ be the exterior angle of each polygon. Take consecutive vertices $P,Q,R,S,T$ of one polygon, where $QR,RS$ lie on the inner boundary. The lines $PQ$ and $TS$ (the shared edges) meet at the centre $O$ of the inner region, and $\angle QOS=\frac{360^\circ}m$.

In quadrilateral $OSRQ$: the angle at $Q$ is $\alpha$ (exterior angle at $Q$ since $O$ is on the extension of $PQ$), likewise at $S$, and at $R$ the angle is $360^\circ-(180^\circ-\alpha)=180^\circ+\alpha$. The angles sum to $360^\circ$:
$$\frac{360}{m}+\alpha+(180+\alpha)+\alpha=360\ \Rightarrow\ 1=\frac2m+\frac6n.$$
So $mn=6m+2n$, i.e. $(m-2)(n-6)=12$. Here $m>2$, so $n-6$ is a positive divisor of $12$: $1,2,3,4,6,12$, giving $n=7,8,9,10,12,18$ (with $m=14,8,6,5,4,3$). Each gives a valid ring.

**Answer: 6**
